Ligand 2 is my current best at Phi 2.3906; ligand 1 is the acetyl probe, whose cyclopropane CH at atom 17 is bonded to the carbonyl at atom 15 - the anchor for the lightest cap. Second-to-last call, and I am staying on the aryl series because it is the only thing in four runs that broke the activity ceiling. An isoxazol-4-yl is the companion to the oxazole I built a moment ago: the same five-membered ring with the same oxygen and nitrogen, but adjacent rather than separated, which changes the dipole and the acceptor geometry while keeping the mass identical at about 320 Da. Having both tells me whether the position cares where the heteroatoms sit in the pendant ring or only that a flat aromatic is present, and it is the lightest pair of candidates in the whole series - 26 Da below my bromine leader and 52 below the phenyl that produced the 0.70. If the aryl effect survives into the azoles at all, one of these two should be the best molecule of the run.
